claim: Environmental cues, such as physical forces and heterotypic cell interactions play a critical role in cell function.
source: Environmental cues, such as physical forces and heterotypic cell interactions play a critical role in cell function, yet their collective contributions to transcriptional changes are unclear.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract about the importance of environmental cues, supported by the overall study design and findings.

claim: Over 43% of the transcriptome was significantly changed by the in vitro environment.
source: Over 43% of the transcriptome was significantly changed by the in vitro environment.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the RNA sequencing analysis comparing cord to culture conditions.

claim: Subjecting cultured cells to long-term shear stress significantly rescued the expression of approximately 17% of genes.
source: Subjecting cultured cells to long-term shear stress significantly rescued the expression of approximately 17% of genes.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the flow experiments comparing static to flow conditions.

claim: Inclusion of heterotypic interactions by co-culture of endothelial cells with smooth muscle cells normalized approximately 9% of the original in vivo signature.
source: Inclusion of heterotypic interactions by co-culture of endothelial cells with smooth muscle cells normalized approximately 9% of the original in vivo signature.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the co-culture experiments.

claim: Endothelial cells define the functional integrity and response to hemodynamic blood forces on the luminal surface of blood vessels.
source: Endothelial cells define the functional integrity and response to hemodynamic blood forces on the luminal surface of blood vessels (Iruela-Arispe and Davis, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Endothelial cells are responsible for the selective trafficking of immune cells, regulation of metabolites and fluid extravasation to tissues.
source: They are also responsible for the selective trafficking of immune cells, regulation of metabolites and fluid extravasation to tissues (Jackson, 2019; Sun and Feinberg, 2015; Vandenbroucke et al., 2008; Wettschureck et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The endothelium provides instructive angiocrine signals required for the differentiation of tissues during development and for homeostasis of organs in the adult.
source: More recently, it has become clear that the endothelium provides instructive angiocrine signals required for the differentiation of tissues during development and for homeostasis of organs in the adult (Gomez-Salinero and Rafii, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Much of the knowledge accumulated on endothelial cell function has emerged through studies in vitro.
source: Much of the knowledge accumulated on endothelial cell function has emerged through studies in vitro.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field, supported by common knowledge and the context of the study.

claim: The ability to grow endothelial cells under culture conditions has enabled investigators to identify growth factors that promote endothelial growth.
source: The ability to grow endothelial cells under culture conditions has enabled investigators to identify growth factors that promote endothelial growth (Apte et al., 2019; Gerber et al., 1998), define the molecules involved in barrier function (Christensen et al., 2016; Corada et al., 2019; Trani and Dejana, 2015), and recognize discrete steps in leukocyte–endothelial selection and extravasation (Muller, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: A complete reductionist in vitro (culture) approach deprives endothelial cells from contextual information which could impact experimental read-outs.
source: However, a complete reductionist in vitro (culture) approach deprives endothelial cells from contextual information which could impact experimental read-outs.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the premise that cells in culture lack environmental cues present in vivo.

claim: The endothelial cell transcriptome is dependent on their native environmental milieu which includes homo- and heterotypic cell interactions, soluble factors, three-dimensional organization, and physical forces.
source: As for all cells, the endothelial cell transcriptome is dependent on their native environmental milieu which includes homo- and heterotypic cell interactions, soluble factors, three-dimensional organization (Wang et al., 2022), and physical forces (Choi and Seo, 2019; Cleuren et al., 2019; Dayang et al., 2019; Jambusaria et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Contextual information is removed when cells are placed in vitro.
source: This contextual information is removed when cells are placed in vitro.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the nature of in vitro culture systems.

claim: While endothelial identity and many biological aspects are retained in culture, there is no frame of reference to determine what has been lost, and what could have been artificially gained, during the transition to an in vitro environment.
source: While endothelial identity and many biological aspects are retained, there is no frame of reference, meaning comparison to in vivo state, to determine what has been lost, and what could have been artificially gained, during the transition to an in vitro environment.
evidence: This is a logical inference that motivates the study design.

claim: Principal component analysis of bulk RNA sequencing transcriptional profiles revealed that cord versus culture/in vitro environments were the dominant factor influencing measured expression levels.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) of bulk RNA sequencing (RNAseq) transcriptional profiles revealed that cord versus culture/in vitro environments were the dominant factor influencing measured expression levels (Figure 1B, C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the PCA analysis shown in Figure 1B and 1C.

claim: PC1 captured 47.4% of the total variance whereas PC2 only accounts for 11.1%.
source: PC1 captured 47.4% of the total variance whereas PC2 only accounts for 11.1%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the PCA analysis.

claim: Approximately half of the expressed genes were differentially expressed between cord and culture conditions (4532–4645 genes overlapping).
source: Approximately half of the expressed genes were differentially expressed between cord and culture conditions (4532–4645 genes overlapping), whereas the transcriptomic signature was very similar between early and late cultures (11,706 genes overlapping) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the differential expression analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The transcriptomic signature was very similar between early and late cultures (11,706 genes overlapping).
source: Approximately half of the expressed genes were differentially expressed between cord and culture conditions (4532–4645 genes overlapping), whereas the transcriptomic signature was very similar between early and late cultures (11,706 genes overlapping) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the differential expression analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: TGFβ and BMP target genes were reduced under culture.
source: Among several signatures, we observed that TGFβ and BMP target genes were reduced under culture.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Some of the most in vivo-specific transcripts were related to the extracellular matrix.
source: Some of the most in vivo-specific transcripts were related to the extracellular matrix; while several genes specific to the in vitro environment associated with the cell cycle (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Several genes specific to the in vitro environment associated with the cell cycle.
source: Some of the most in vivo-specific transcripts were related to the extracellular matrix; while several genes specific to the in vitro environment associated with the cell cycle (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Endothelial cells lose expression of flow-responsive genes (KLF4, KLF2) once placed under culture conditions.
source: As expected, we found that endothelial cells lose expression of flow-responsive genes (KLF4, KLF2) once placed under culture conditions, whereas they quickly acquire proliferation-related genes (CCNB2, CCNA2, CDCA2).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Endothelial cells quickly acquire proliferation-related genes (CCNB2, CCNA2, CDCA2) in culture.
source: As expected, we found that endothelial cells lose expression of flow-responsive genes (KLF4, KLF2) once placed under culture conditions, whereas they quickly acquire proliferation-related genes (CCNB2, CCNA2, CDCA2).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Transition into culture promotes a significant decrease in transcripts associated with extracellular matrix genes (COL23A1, MMP28, FBLN2, ELN, COL1A2, COL6A3).
source: Perhaps more surprising was that transition into culture promotes a significant decrease in transcripts associated with extracellular matrix genes (COL23A1, MMP28, FBLN2, ELN, COL1A2, COL6A3), cytokine (CXCL2, SOCS3, TGFB3, CTGF), and early response genes (FOS, ZFP36, JUNB) (Supplementary file 1, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Transition into culture promotes a significant decrease in transcripts associated with cytokine genes (CXCL2, SOCS3, TGFB3, CTGF).
source: Perhaps more surprising was that transition into culture promotes a significant decrease in transcripts associated with extracellular matrix genes (COL23A1, MMP28, FBLN2, ELN, COL1A2, COL6A3), cytokine (CXCL2, SOCS3, TGFB3, CTGF), and early response genes (FOS, ZFP36, JUNB) (Supplementary file 1, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Transition into culture promotes a significant decrease in transcripts associated with early response genes (FOS, ZFP36, JUNB).
source: Perhaps more surprising was that transition into culture promotes a significant decrease in transcripts associated with extracellular matrix genes (COL23A1, MMP28, FBLN2, ELN, COL1A2, COL6A3), cytokine (CXCL2, SOCS3, TGFB3, CTGF), and early response genes (FOS, ZFP36, JUNB) (Supplementary file 1, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Transcripts associated with survival and a pro-angiogenic phenotype were upregulated in culture (e.g., APLN, BAX, CCN, CCNB2, CCNBA1, CEPH1, CDCA7l, CDCA2, MDM2).
source: In addition to increased expression of cell cycle genes in culture, transcripts associated with survival and a pro-angiogenic phenotype were also upregulated (e.g., APLN, BAX, CCN, CCNB2, CCNBA1, CEPH1, CDCA7l, CDCA2, MDM2).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: The significant increase of VEPH1 under culture conditions was of particular interest as the protein product of this gene is associated with suppression of TGFβ1, FOXO, and Wnt signaling.
source: Further, the significant increase of VEPH1 under culture conditions was of particular interest as the protein product of this gene is associated with suppression of TGFβ1, FOXO, and Wnt signaling (Shathasivam et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis, with the functional interpretation supported by a citation.

claim: PCA analysis of relative protein abundances demonstrated clear separation of cord and in vitro culture experimental conditions.
source: PCA analysis of relative protein abundances was conducted for seven matched individuals from the cord and early culture. The analysis demonstrated clear separation of the experimental conditions (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics PCA analysis shown in Figure 1H.

claim: There were significant changes in protein expression between cord and culture environments.
source: In agreement to the RNA-level differences, there were significant changes in protein expression between the environments.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis.

claim: About 160/3000 proteins were specific to cord.
source: Albeit not as remarkably different than the transcriptomic read-outs (likely due to depth of coverage and statistical power), we identified an -omics signature of proteins specific to cord (about 160/3000 proteins) and to early culture (about 411/3000 proteins) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the proteomics analysis.

claim: About 411/3000 proteins were specific to early culture.
source: Albeit not as remarkably different than the transcriptomic read-outs (likely due to depth of coverage and statistical power), we identified an -omics signature of proteins specific to cord (about 160/3000 proteins) and to early culture (about 411/3000 proteins) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the proteomics analysis.

claim: The relationships between t-statistics between cord and culture across -omic layers revealed significant correlation between RNA and protein signatures (r = 0.4, p = 1 × 10−07).
source: The relationships between t-statistics between cord and culture across -omic layers revealed significant correlation between RNA and protein signatures (r = 0.4, p = 1 × 10−07) (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The data revealed low expression of cell cycle proteins and high expression of flow-responsive proteins in the cord (ex vivo) proteomics profile.
source: Consistent with prior findings, the data revealed low expression of cell cycle proteins and high expression of flow-responsive proteins in the cord (ex vivo) proteomics profile (Figure 1I, Supplementary files 2 and 9).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Once placed under laminar flow, endothelial cells significantly change their morphology and reduce proliferation resembling in vivo conditions.
source: This approach is warranted by observations that once placed under laminar flow, endothelial cells significantly change their morphology and reduce proliferation resembling in vivo conditions (Chiu and Chien, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The onset of flow is associated with significant transcriptional increase in flow-responsive genes, like KLF2.
source: Further, the onset of flow is associated with significant transcriptional increase in flow-responsive genes, like KLF2 (Chien, 2007; Nakajima and Mochizuki, 2017; Zhou et al., 2014), which is one of the cord-specific transcripts (Figures 1 and 2, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature and confirmed by the current study's data.

claim: PCA of matched patients demonstrated static cells in vitro and under 30 min of flow displayed relatively similar global transcriptional signatures.
source: First, PCA of matched patients (n = 4, Table 1) demonstrated static cells in vitro and under 30 min of flow displayed relatively similar global transcriptional signatures.
evidence: This is a finding from the PCA analysis of flow experiments.

claim: Differences were apparent on PC1 with flow, defined as 8–48 hr of laminar shear stress exposure.
source: Differences were apparent on PC1 with flow, defined as 8–48 hr of laminar shear stress exposure (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the PCA analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Progressive time under flow from up to 48 hr of shear stress revealed that the transcriptional signature of cells correlates more specifically to that of the cord than with static cultures.
source: Progressive time under flow from up to 48 hr of shear stress (flow) revealed that the transcriptional signature of cells correlates more specifically to that of the cord than with static cultures.
evidence: This is a finding from the time-course flow analysis.

claim: By 48 hr of shear stress the correlational coefficient to cord reached r = 0.34, p = −8.0 × 10−9, which is significantly different than static culture.
source: Initially, the correlation coefficient was insignificant (r = −0.035, p = 0.004) with progressive changes to the point that by 48 hr of shear stress the correlational coefficient to cord reached r = 0.34, = −8.0 × 10−9, which is significantly different than static culture (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: GO terms associated with blood vessel development (EDN1, BMP2, BMP4, TGFPR3, ITG1BP1, HES1, HEY1) were regained by long-term exposure to flow.
source: Specifically, GO terms associated with blood vessel development (EDN1, BMP2, BMP4, TGFPR3, ITG1BP1, HES1, HEY1), regulation of cellular protein location (ITGA3, RACK1, PTPN9, SPTBN1), and cellular response to laminar fluid shear stress (ASS1, KLF2, KLF4, MAPK7, NFE2L2) were regained by long-term exposure to flow (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a finding from the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: GO terms associated with regulation of cellular protein location (ITGA3, RACK1, PTPN9, SPTBN1) were regained by long-term exposure to flow.
source: Specifically, GO terms associated with blood vessel development (EDN1, BMP2, BMP4, TGFPR3, ITG1BP1, HES1, HEY1), regulation of cellular protein location (ITGA3, RACK1, PTPN9, SPTBN1), and cellular response to laminar fluid shear stress (ASS1, KLF2, KLF4, MAPK7, NFE2L2) were regained by long-term exposure to flow (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a finding from the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: GO terms associated with cellular response to laminar fluid shear stress (ASS1, KLF2, KLF4, MAPK7, NFE2L2) were regained by long-term exposure to flow.
source: Specifically, GO terms associated with blood vessel development (EDN1, BMP2, BMP4, TGFPR3, ITG1BP1, HES1, HEY1), regulation of cellular protein location (ITGA3, RACK1, PTPN9, SPTBN1), and cellular response to laminar fluid shear stress (ASS1, KLF2, KLF4, MAPK7, NFE2L2) were regained by long-term exposure to flow (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a finding from the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Gene set enrichment analysis of differential expressed genes in cultured endothelial cells under flow (vs. static) revealed gene annotations related to an acute inflammatory response, heart morphogenesis, second messenger-mediated signaling, and ossification.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis of differential expressed genes in cultured endothelial cells under flow (vs. static) revealed gene annotations related to an acute inflammatory response, heart morphogenesis, second messenger-mediated signaling, and ossification (related to BMP and TGFβ responses).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene set enrichment analysis.

claim: tRNA and rRNA metabolic processes were silenced under flow.
source: We also found tRNA and rRNA metabolic processes were silenced under flow (Supplementary files 3 and 4, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene set enrichment analysis.

claim: The incorporation of shear stress to the in vitro static conditions attenuated the variability between cord and culture with a drift recovery in 17% of the genes.
source: Specifically, the incorporation of shear stress to the in vitro static conditions attenuated the variability between cord and culture with a drift recovery in 17% of the genes (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the integrated analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: WGCNA identified 36 co-expression modules.
source: To identify cohorts of genes altered by shear stress and that approximate the in vivo environment (rescued), we performed a transcriptome-wide weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). This approach led us to identify 36 co-expression modules, revealing gene groups that are co-enriched in either cord or culture environments, or in static versus flow conditions (Figure 3C, red: down; blue: up, Supplementary files 3 and 4, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the WGCNA analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The blue module (2185 genes, r = 0.71, p = 3e−04) was increased in the cord and under flow conditions as compared to static culture.
source: The blue module (2185 genes, r = 0 .71, p = 3e−04) was increased in the cord and under flow conditions as compared to static culture.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the WGCNA analysis.

claim: The blue module showed increased transcriptional concurrence with the cord and this was progressive with time under flow (r = 0.8, p = 4e−04).
source: The blue module showed increased transcriptional concurrence with the cord and this was progressive with time under flow (r = 0.8, p = 4e−04).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the WGCNA analysis.

claim: The genes and GOs associated with the blue module included blood vessel development and leukocyte activation.
source: Notably, the genes and GOs associated with this module included blood vessel development and leukocyte activation (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a finding from the GO enrichment analysis of the blue module shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The brown module was decreased both in the cord and in flow as compared to static cells (1408 genes, r = −0.9, p = 3e−08).
source: The brown module was decreased both in the cord and in flow as compared to static cells (1408 genes, r = −0.9, p = 3e−08).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the WGCNA analysis.

claim: The brown module was defined by cell cycle and cell cycle checkpoints, was less expressed in cord (vs. culture) and in flow (vs. static, r = −0.62, p = 0.01).
source: The brown module was defined by cell cycle and cell cycle checkpoints, was less expressed in cord (vs. culture) and in flow (vs. static, r = −0.62, p = 0.01).
evidence: This is a finding from the WGCNA analysis.

claim: Unsupervised clustering demonstrated the cells cluster by origin.
source: Unsupervised clustering demonstrated the cells cluster by origin (Figure 5B–E).
evidence: This is a finding from the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 5B-E.

claim: Co-culture prompted a reduction in NOTCH target genes (FABP4, GJA4, FABP5, HEY).
source: Specifically, co-culture prompted a reduction in NOTCH target genes (FABP4, GJA4, FABP5, HEY) and a clear induction in TGFβ downstream targets (SERPINE1, IGFBP7, SOX4, TIMP1) (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a finding from the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Co-culture prompted a clear induction in TGFβ downstream targets (SERPINE1, IGFBP7, SOX4, TIMP1).
source: Specifically, co-culture prompted a reduction in NOTCH target genes (FABP4, GJA4, FABP5, HEY) and a clear induction in TGFβ downstream targets (SERPINE1, IGFBP7, SOX4, TIMP1) (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a finding from the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The major signaling pathways and transcriptional regulators that prompted transcriptional drifts on endothelial cells by co-culture included TGFβ, VEGF, TP53, HTT, MYC, TNF, EDN1, SP1, and HGF.
source: As shown in Figure 5G, the major signaling pathways and transcriptional regulators that prompted transcriptional drifts on endothelial cells by co-culture included TGFβ, VEGF, TP53, HTT, MYC, TNF, EDN1, SP1, and HGF.
evidence: This is a finding from the Ingenuity pathway analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claim: A module score using the expression of downstream targets for TFGβ1 and VEGFA showed a significant increase upon co-culture for both.
source: We calculated a module score using the expression of downstream targets for TFGβ1 and VEGFA identified by ingenuity pathway analysis and found a significant increase upon co-culture for both (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is a finding from the module score analysis shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Co-culture conditions resulted in an increase of clathrin-related genes (AAK1, AP2B1, and CLTB).
source: Interestingly, co-culture conditions resulted in an increase of clathrin-related genes (AAK1, AP2B1, and CLTB) and a decrease in caveolin-related genes (CAV1 and CAV2) (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is a finding from the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 5J.

claim: Co-culture conditions resulted in a decrease in caveolin-related genes (CAV1 and CAV2).
source: Interestingly, co-culture conditions resulted in an increase of clathrin-related genes (AAK1, AP2B1, and CLTB) and a decrease in caveolin-related genes (CAV1 and CAV2) (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is a finding from the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 5J.

claim: These changes occurred with no significant alterations in CDH5, ERG, NOTCH1, and JAG1.
source: These changes occurred with no significant alterations in CDH5, ERG, NOTCH1, and JAG1 (Figure 5K).
evidence: This is a finding from the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 5K.

claim: Global transcriptional profiling in UMAP showed a shift of co-culture toward cord.
source: Interestingly, global transcriptional profiling in uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) showed a shift of co-culture toward cord (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from the UMAP analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Genes rescued by co-culture relate to NOTCH signaling (HES1, FABP4) and TGFβ (ENG).
source: Examples of those categories are shown in Figure 6D and group analysis by dot blot as displayed in Figure 6E. Genes rescued by co-culture relate to NOTCH signaling (HES1, FABP4) and TGFβ (ENG).
evidence: This is a finding from the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 6D and 6E.

claim: Clathrin pathways, noted to be increased by SMC co-culture, were indeed part of the in vivo signature displayed by endothelial cells in the cord with upregulation of transcripts for AAK1 and EPN2.
source: In addition, we found that clathrin pathways, noted to be increased by SMC co-culture (Figure 5) were indeed part of the in vivo signature displayed by endothelial cells in the cord (Figure 6F) with upregulation of transcripts for AAK1 and EPN2.
evidence: This is a finding from the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Co-culture was responsible for rescue of TJP1, responsible for tight junctions and two transmembrane proteins that regulate calcium homeostasis (TMEM165 and 203).
source: Co-culture also was responsible for rescue of TJP1, responsible for tight junctions and two transmembrane proteins that regulate calcium homeostasis (TMEM165 and 203) (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is a finding from the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Co-culture of endothelial cells with SMCs normalized networks related to cell growth and differentiation, clathrin-vesicle-related genes, and recovered targets downstream TGFβ, recovering approximately 9% of the original cord (in vivo) signature.
source: In summary, co-culture of endothelial cells with SMCs normalized networks related to cell growth and differentiation, clathrin-vesicle-related genes, and recovered targets downstream TGFβ, recovering approximately 9% of the original cord (in vivo) signature (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary finding from the co-culture experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: Endothelial cells are characterized by a unique set of genes collectively referred to identity genes (i.e., CDH5, PECAM1, ERG).
source: Endothelial cells are characterized by a unique set of genes collectively referred to identity genes (i.e., CDH5, PECAM1, ERG) and a group of genes whose expression level varies according to stressors and environmental conditions.
evidence: This is a general statement about endothelial cell biology supported by established knowledge.

claim: A major adaptation that cells must acquire when placed in culture relates to cell proliferation.
source: A major adaptation that cells must acquire when placed in culture relates to cell proliferation.
evidence: This is a general statement about cell culture biology supported by established knowledge.

claim: High levels of transcripts related to cell cycle, mitosis, and DNA repair mechanisms are still present at confluency and represent the single most significant alteration when comparing freshly isolated cells to genetically identical cohorts in vitro.
source: Nonetheless, we demonstrate that high levels of transcripts related to cell cycle, mitosis, and DNA repair mechanisms are still present at confluency and represent the single most significant alteration when comparing freshly isolated cells to genetically identical cohorts in vitro.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: There are significant alterations in cytoskeletal dynamics and focal adhesions that are artificially elevated in vitro, compared to ex vivo.
source: Similarly, there are significant alterations in cytoskeletal dynamics and focal adhesions that are artificially elevated in vitro, compared to ex vivo.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Recapitulating the native flow seen by endothelial cells by exposure of static cultures to shear stress resulted in a significant shift toward ex vivo (freshly isolated cells) signature.
source: Recapitulating the native flow seen by endothelial cells by exposure of static cultures to shear stress resulted in a significant shift toward ex vivo (freshly isolated cells) signature.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the flow experiments.

claim: Two major pathways and their downstream genes were regained by long-term flow: BMP and NOTCH signaling.
source: Specifically, we found that two major pathways and their downstream genes were regained by long-term flow: BMP and NOTCH signaling.
evidence: This is a finding from the flow experiments.

claim: Several SMAD targets were rescued by incorporating long-term flow into cultures.
source: Indeed, several SMAD targets were rescued by incorporating long-term flow into cultures.
evidence: This is a finding from the flow experiments.

claim: BMP signaling is significantly potentiated by flow.
source: Importantly, it has been recently shown that BMP signaling is significantly potentiated by flow (Baeyens et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: NOTCH target genes (HES, HEY) regained levels similar to those captured in freshly isolated preparations.
source: Similarly, NOTCH target genes (HES, HEY) regained levels similar to those captured in freshly isolated preparations.
evidence: This is a finding from the flow experiments.

claim: NOTCH signaling was increased by flow and mechanosensing.
source: These findings are congruent with recent studies demonstrating that NOTCH signaling was increased by flow and mechanosensing (Mack et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: An unexpected GO signature regained by shear stress included proteins associated with cellular localization, such as ITPR1, IGFBP5, DLL1, among others.
source: An unexpected GO signature regained by shear stress included proteins associated with cellular localization, such as ITPR1, IGFBP5, DLL1, among others, highlighting the role of laminar shear stress in endothelial cell polarity.
evidence: This is a finding from the GO enrichment analysis of flow experiments.

claim: Alterations in junctional proteins and cytoskeletal architecture were recovered in endothelial cell–SMC co-cultures.
source: Alterations in junctional proteins and cytoskeletal architecture were recovered in endothelial cell–SMC co-cultures.
evidence: This is a finding from the co-culture experiments.

claim: Co-culture of endothelial cells with SMCs induced TGFβ downstream targets in the endothelium, including several extracellular matrix proteins and integrins.
source: Co-culture of endothelial cells with SMCs also induced TGFβ downstream targets in the endothelium, including several extracellular matrix proteins and integrins which brought further alignment to the in vivo transcriptome.
evidence: This is a finding from the co-culture experiments.

claim: SMCs significantly reduced the prominent proliferative signature of endothelial cells and promoted a partial recovery in endothelial cell differentiation.
source: In addition, SMCs significantly reduced the prominent proliferative signature of endothelial cells and promoted a partial recovery in endothelial cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a finding from the co-culture experiments.

claim: Co-culture recovered ENG and integrins regulated by TGFB1 (ITGB1, ITGA1, ITGA5), as well as several extracellular membrane proteins (COL1A1, FN1, TIMP1, SERPINE1).
source: Specifically, this included ENG and integrins regulated by TGFB1 (ITGB1, ITGA1, ITGA5), as well as several extracellular membrane proteins (COL1A1, FN1, TIMP1, SERPINE1) (Gallicchio et al., 1994; Nackman et al., 1996; Powell et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a finding from the co-culture experiments, with the functional interpretation supported by citations.

claim: Loss of architecture in vitro could induce the loss of expression of acute phase transcripts, as seen with injury of the aorta in vivo.
source: It can be postulated that loss of architecture in vitro could induce the loss of expression of acute phase transcripts, as seen with injury of the aorta in vivo (Shirali et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Endothelial-heterotypic crosstalk have been shown essential during development and altered in vascular pathologies such as aneurysms.
source: These endothelial-heterotypic crosstalk have been shown essential during development and altered in vascular pathologies such as aneurysms (Boezio et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Exposing endothelial cells to culture conditions does not appear to significantly affect cellular identity.
source: Exposing endothelial cells to culture conditions does not appear to significantly affect cellular identity.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Transcriptional levels of CDH5, PECAM1, ERG, Claudins, Sox(s), and other so-called endothelial markers were not significantly impacted by culture.
source: Transcriptional levels of CDH5, PECAM1, ERG, Claudins, Sox(s), and other so-called endothelial markers were not significantly impacted.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: ERG is essential for regulation of CDH5, VWF, and NOS3 as well as a hallmark of endothelial cell lineage.
source: ERG is essential for regulation of CDH5, VWF, and NOS3 as well as a hallmark of endothelial cell lineage (Birdsey et al., 2008; Laumonnier et al., 2000; Nikolova-Krstevski et al., 2009; Shah et al., 2016; Yuan et al., 2009).

claim: 26% out the 43% of transcriptional alterations could not be recovered by either shear stress (which rescued 17% of the changes) or by contact with SMCs (that rescued 9% of the changes).
